title: How many zeros end three thousand squared, and is it odd or even?
description: The video squares three thousand and counts the zeros at the end, then decides if the square is odd or even. Keeko doubts the count after thinking the square has the same number of zeros as the number.
teaching_notes: One idea: when a number ends in zeros, its square ends in twice as many zeros. An even number has an even square. Watch for students who count the zeros of the number and forget to double them.

source: How many zeros end 3000², and is 3000² odd or even?
video_script.why: The child sees that the zeros of a number double in its square, and that the square of an even number is even.
video_script.substitution: Count the zeros of the number, add the same count again, and decide odd or even from the number itself.
video_script.anchor: the number three thousand written large with a square sign
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko counts the three zeros of three thousand and stops, saying only three zeros. The number is multiplied by itself, so its zeros are counted twice, six in all.
video_script.payoff_line: Three thousand squared ends in six zeros, and it is even

final_answer.spoken: six zeros, and three thousand squared is even

never_show: the 30² or 3000² answer in the exercise videos
maths_rules: 10² = 100 (1 zero doubles to 2), 20² = 400, 200² = 40000 (2 zeros double to 4)
3000 is even, and even × even is even, so 3000² is even; it also ends in 0, which is even
check: 300² = 90000, 300 has 2 zeros and 90000 has 4 zeros
the slip: 3 zeros only counts one of the two factors of 3000 × 3000
video_script.design: One idea: zeros in the number double in the square. Wrong idea: the square keeps the same number of zeros. The number stays in the anchor band.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='num'/>Take the number three thousand and square it.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many zeros end the square, and is the square odd or even?

beats.on_screen: the question holds still and the two empty boxes glow

marks.stop: the two empty boxes glow in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 10² = 100, 20² = 400, 200² = 40000 with the zeros at the end in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='ten'/>Ten times ten is one hundred. Ten has one zero, and one hundred has two.
<bookmark mark='twenty'/>Twenty times twenty is four hundred, with two zeros.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Two hundred times two hundred is forty thousand. Two zeros turn into four.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the number is three thousand, and we square it.

beats.on_screen: To find: the zeros at the end of 3000², and odd or even

marks.find: the two things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many zeros end the square, and if it is odd or even.

marks.split: 3000 splits into 3 and 1000 in each factor

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, write three thousand as three times one thousand, twice.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Three times three is nine.
<bookmark mark='million'/>One thousand times one thousand is one million, so the square is nine million.
<bookmark mark='each'/>Step two, each three thousand ends in three zeros.
<bookmark mark='add'/>The zeros of the two numbers add up, three and three, which is six.

marks.rule: the line even × even = even appears

narration: <bookmark mark='even'/>Step three, three thousand is an even number.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>An even number times an even number is even, so the square is even.

marks.check: 300 × 300 = 90000 is written and its zeros are counted against the two zeros of 300

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check with a smaller number. Three hundred times three hundred is ninety thousand. Its four zeros are twice the two zeros of three hundred.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Three thousand squared ends in six zeros, and it is even.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 3000 has 3 zeros, so 3 zeros; the second 3000 appears and the count becomes 3 + 3

marks.second: the second 3000 slides in beside the first

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the square has only three zeros, because three thousand has three.
<bookmark mark='second'/>But three thousand is multiplied by three thousand, so there are two such numbers.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Both bring their zeros, which makes six.
